title: Model a diverging journey as an interlocking: a declared artifact-keyed registry selecting the next linear train

facts.note: Task text names a branching journey or train routing.
Planner artifacts that declare trains and their dispatch; a file-kind cue alone is not sufficient activation.

values: journey gains a divergence point / branch between trains
facts.note: Whether a journey actually diverges is a semantic judgment over the plan; no detector exists (this node is an advisory anchor bound to no validator).

fires: Planner decomposes a journey whose next step depends on which artifact was produced (one outcome continues to one train, another outcome to a different train).
Planner authors or edits a dispatch map that selects a train from a produced artifact URN.
Planner is tempted to add a conditional branch inside a train to handle a diverging journey.
doesNotFire: A strictly linear journey that is fully served by a single train with no divergence.
Coder/tester work implementing the route-control runner or its dispatcher (runtime realization, governed by coder/tester conventions).
Plans that do not involve trains or journey routing at all.

given: A planned journey diverges: which train runs next depends on an artifact produced earlier.
when: The planner decomposes the journey into trains and records how the branch is routed.
then: Declare the branch as an interlocking: a domain-owned, schema-valid routing registry (artifact_urn -> train_id) keyed by the produced artifact (the divergence signal), composing strictly-linear trains into a branching journey-of-journeys.
prefer: Key dispatch by one produced artifact URN; a composite (urn, discriminant) key is exceptional (planner.train.dispatch-map-is-registry, planner.train.dispatch-composite-key-exceptional).
Keep trains linear; branch between trains, in the interlocking (planner.train.linearity).
Name only the routing decision; leave the route-control runner and dispatcher to coder/tester.
avoid: Expressing the dispatch map as code or an imperative map.
Specifying runner/dispatcher mechanics in planner artifacts.
Treating this definition as an enforced check; enforcement lives in the constraint/rule nodes that require it.
why: An interlocking gives a diverging journey a stable meaning: the routing decision is a declared, artifact-keyed registry rather than branching inside trains, so trains stay linear.
evidence: Reviewer finds, for each divergence point in a journey, a declared registry entry artifact_urn -> train_id owned by the domain and valid against its schema.
Reviewer confirms each train composed by the interlocking is linear (no internal branching).
Any composite (urn, discriminant) key is justified as exceptional per planner.train.dispatch-composite-key-exceptional.

Compliance is established transitively through the enforceable constraint/rule nodes that require this anchor (e.g. planner.train.dispatch-map-is-registry, planner.train.dispatch-composite-key-exceptional, planner.train.linearity); this node has no validator of its own.
verifier_detail: Advisory semantic anchor: not bound to any validator; produce no direct findings from this node. Semantic anchor = a definitional node giving the artifact a stable meaning, transitively protected by the enforceable constraint/rule nodes that require it.

Term decomposition: interlocking -> {routing-decision, artifact-keyed, declared-registry, train-composing}. routing-decision: selects the next train when a journey diverges rather than branching inside a train (trains stay linear, see planner.train.linearity). artifact-keyed: dispatch keyed by produced artifact URN; composite (urn, discriminant) key exceptional (planner.train.dispatch-map-is-registry, planner.train.dispatch-composite-key-exceptional). declared-registry: dispatch map is a declared, schema-valid, domain-owned registry, not code. train-composing: sequences multiple linear trains into a branching journey-of-journeys.

Runtime realization enforcers (route-control runner exists / delegates execution / carries no cargo / bilateral binding) live in the coder+tester layer (atdd.extension.coder.train-interlocking and atdd.extension.tester.train-interlocking), not here.
audit: Term ids/labels: semantic_anchor ('Advisory semantic anchor'); interlocking ('Interlocking').

Runtime enforcers in atdd.extension.coder.train-interlocking and atdd.extension.tester.train-interlocking are related to this domain anchor by cross-persona traceability, tracked as a separate follow-up, not authored here.
